userStories.title: Split global stylesheet into layered sources
userStories.description: Refactor the oversized global stylesheet by moving theme tokens, shared utilities, and animation rules into imported style files while keeping `src/app/globals.css` as the single app entrypoint.
acceptanceCriteria: `src/app/globals.css` becomes materially smaller and mostly coordinates imports
Theme variables, utility class names, and animation classes continue to resolve without regressions
The new style file split makes color tokens easier to audit separately from utilities and effects

userStories.title: Normalize spinner variants to CSS variable tokens
userStories.description: Update the shared loading spinner to remove hardcoded Tailwind color classes, replace the `violet`/`purple` drift with a consistent semantic API, and keep overlay/message helpers aligned with repo token rules.
acceptanceCriteria: Spinner variants use CSS variables or shared color utilities instead of hardcoded Tailwind colors
The public variant API is internally consistent and documented in the file comments/types
Existing spinner callers keep working or have a clear codemod-level migration path

userStories.title: Tokenize default error boundary UI
userStories.description: Remove remaining hardcoded error colors and CTA styles from the shared error boundary so fallback UIs inherit the same semantic color system as the rest of the app.
acceptanceCriteria: Default and inline error states use CSS variables or shared button/color helpers only
Retry CTA styling is consistent with shared interactive tokens
Development-only error details remain available without reintroducing hardcoded colors

userStories.title: Remove remaining hardcoded colors from design tokens
userStories.description: Audit the centralized design token file and replace any raw Tailwind color classes or mixed token strategies with CSS-variable-backed values that match `globals.css` and `src/lib/colors.ts`.
acceptanceCriteria: `src/lib/design-tokens.ts` contains no hardcoded Tailwind color classes for semantic UI states
Token names align with the existing purple/orange/status variable system
Shared token consumers can keep importing from one source without behavioral changes

userStories.title: Extract scrollable page shell from section orchestration
userStories.description: Break `src/app/scrollable/page.tsx` into smaller pieces by moving the local error boundary and section-loading shell into reusable app or UI modules, leaving the page focused on route composition.
acceptanceCriteria: The page file falls well below the current size and primarily wires together imported sections
Local error/loading helpers are moved into reusable modules instead of being defined inline
Scroll behavior, modal state, and reduced-motion behavior remain unchanged

userStories.title: Create a reusable lazy-panel fallback component
userStories.description: Introduce a shared loading primitive for dynamic module fallbacks so app routes stop defining near-duplicate loading markup inline.
acceptanceCriteria: The new component supports the fallback patterns currently duplicated in `src/app/page.tsx` and `src/app/scrollable/page.tsx`
Fallback visuals use shared icons, tokens, and loading primitives instead of ad hoc markup
Route-level dynamic imports become thinner after adopting the new primitive

userStories.title: Extract chat domain types and persistence helpers
userStories.description: Move message typing and localStorage serialization logic out of the monolithic chat component into dedicated chat modules so persistence can be tested independently from rendering.
acceptanceCriteria: Chat message and callback contracts live in dedicated type definitions instead of inside the UI file
Storage helpers are isolated from rendering and remain responsible for validation/slicing behavior
The main chat component stops owning low-level persistence details directly

userStories.title: Extract chat request/session side effects into a hook
userStories.description: Create a focused hook for message submission, timeout handling, analytics, and feedback calls so the main chat component becomes a thin orchestrator rather than a state machine plus UI file.
acceptanceCriteria: Network requests, abort/timeout behavior, and analytics are encapsulated in a dedicated hook
The hook exposes a narrow public API that the main chat UI can consume without reaching into implementation details
The main chat component becomes materially smaller and easier to reason about

userStories.title: Split chat presentation into focused subcomponents
userStories.description: Move message list, message actions, quick actions, and input form rendering into dedicated presentational files while keeping the exported chat entrypoint stable for current imports.
acceptanceCriteria: The default-export chat entrypoint keeps its external API stable for existing route imports
Rendering concerns are separated into focused subcomponents instead of one 500+ line file
Each subcomponent has a clear responsibility and receives typed props only for the state it needs

userStories.title: Add a root barrel for the Dimension feature
userStories.description: Create a stable public API for the Dimension feature so route imports stop reaching into individual implementation files and future internal splits stay hidden behind one entrypoint.
acceptanceCriteria: Dimension exports are available from a single root barrel
App routes can import the main viewer and public types without referencing internal file names
The new barrel defines a clear public surface for future scene/UI refactors

userStories.title: Extract Dimension scene primitives from the 3D module
userStories.description: Split the 3D implementation into smaller scene-focused components such as controls, fallback geometry, and model wrappers so `Dimension.3d.tsx` stops owning every render path directly.
acceptanceCriteria: The 3D file is reduced to scene composition rather than containing every mesh/control implementation inline
Extracted scene primitives receive narrowly typed props and preserve current SSR-disabled usage
Existing model loading, wireframe, and fallback behavior remain intact after the split

userStories.title: Extract Dimension controller state from the main viewer
userStories.description: Move fullscreen, model selection, viewport state, keyboard wiring, and toast-facing control logic into a dedicated controller hook so the main viewer file can focus on composition.
acceptanceCriteria: The main Dimension component becomes a thin composition layer around hooks and UI pieces
Cross-cutting side effects like resize handling and keyboard control setup are isolated from JSX rendering
Public props and user-visible viewer controls behave the same after refactoring

userStories.title: Move boot sequence timing logic into a dedicated hook
userStories.description: Extract the boot screen phase machine, timers, and cleanup into a reusable hook so the visual component focuses on presentation and animation markup rather than lifecycle bookkeeping.
acceptanceCriteria: Boot timing constants and phase transitions are encapsulated outside the JSX-heavy screen component
Timer setup and cleanup are easier to test and reason about independently
The exported `BootScreen` behavior and callbacks remain unchanged for `src/app/page.tsx`

userStories.title: Extract header actions and link configuration
userStories.description: Reduce the size and branching inside `Header.tsx` by moving link metadata and action wiring into dedicated helpers while keeping the visual shell focused on rendering and responsive layout.
acceptanceCriteria: Link/action metadata no longer lives inline beside responsive rendering logic
Clipboard, toast, theme, and analytics behavior remain explicit but less entangled with JSX
The header file drops below the current size threshold without changing its public props

userStories.title: Tokenize ReactionGame state styling
userStories.description: Replace hardcoded gameplay state gradients and raw white opacity classes with named token mappings or shared design helpers so the reaction game follows the repo color rules.
acceptanceCriteria: Gameplay state colors are expressed through semantic token mappings rather than hardcoded Tailwind colors
The file no longer mixes several ad hoc color systems for status visuals and instructional text
The game remains visually distinct without violating the repo's color-source-of-truth rules

userStories.title: Tokenize shared result screen feedback states
userStories.description: Audit the shared playground result screen and replace remaining hardcoded success/share colors with semantic status tokens so every game result view inherits the same maintainable color system.
acceptanceCriteria: Success and share feedback states use semantic token-backed classes only
Shared playground UI stays visually consistent across games after the token cleanup
The result screen remains reusable and does not introduce game-specific style assumptions

userStories.title: Add regression tests for shared UI tokenized states
userStories.description: Introduce focused component tests for shared loading and error primitives so token/API cleanups can be refactored safely without silent UI regressions.
acceptanceCriteria: Tests cover the supported spinner variants and rendered accessibility labels/messages
Tests verify the error boundary retry path and default fallback rendering behavior
Shared UI token refactors have guardrails beyond lint/build success

userStories.title: Document repo maintainability rules for future contributors
userStories.description: Write a concise contributor-facing guide that encodes the maintainability rules for file size, styling sources, client/server boundaries, barrel exports, and when to extract hooks or shared primitives.
acceptanceCriteria: The guide covers the repo's existing color-token and Three.js SSR conventions explicitly
It gives contributors a concrete checklist for deciding when to split files or extract shared modules
The documentation is short enough to be used in normal development rather than ignored
